mainTopic: Saying ברכות for others after fulfilling one's own obligation, and blowing שופר when ראש השנה falls on שבת
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a topic from earlier on the דף. Food ברכות can only be said for others by someone who is eating too, while ברכות of a מצוה can be said for others anytime. The גמרא asks about the ברכה on the מצה at the סדר and the wine of קידוש, and a story about רב פפי shows that the wine ברכה of קידוש can be said for others. A ברייתא sums up the rules, and the פרק ראוהו בית דין ends with a הדרן. The new פרק opens with a משנה: when ראש השנה falls on שבת, the שופר was blown only in the מקדש, and after the חורבן רבן יוחנן בן זכאי set up blowing in places with a בית דין. רבא shows that the Torah allows blowing on שבת, and the רבנן forbade it in case someone carries the שופר to an expert, the same reason given for לולב and מגילה. A ברייתא then tells how רבן יוחנן בן זכאי had the שופר blown in יבנה before בני בתירה could debate it. Finally, the גמרא explains how the חכמים differ from the תנא קמא about a temporary בית דין, and begins a comment from רב הונא that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The bread of מצה and the wine of קידוש: can one say the blessing for others?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברכה on the bread of מצה and the ברכה on the wine of קידוש can be said for others by someone who already fulfilled his own obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for the ברכה on the bread of מצה and the ברכה on the wine of קידוש? Since these are part of an obligation, can a person say them for others? Or perhaps the ברכה itself is not the obligation, so he cannot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about two food ברכות that are connected to a מצוה, מצה and קידוש wine. It asks whether they follow the rule for food ברכות or the rule for מצוה ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone who is not eating cannot say a food ברכה for others. Here, though, the eating of מצה and the wine of קידוש are required, so maybe their ברכות count as part of a חובה and anyone can say them for others. The other side of the question is that the actual חובה is the eating or drinking, while the ברכה is still just a food ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the day holy, which means קידוש on שבת or יום טוב
He takes others out of their obligation, the same as מוציא
Or perhaps, which introduces the other side of a question

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether מצה or קידוש is a מצוה. Everyone agrees they are. The question is only whether the ברכה on the food is part of that חובה.

phrases.english: The blessing over the bread of matzah,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִרְכַּת הַיַּיִן שֶׁל קִידּוּשׁ הַיּוֹם, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and the blessing over the wine of the day's kiddush, what is the law?
Since it is an obligation, can he discharge others?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: בְּרָכָה לָאו חוֹבָה הִיא.
phrases.english: Or perhaps the blessing itself is not an obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ? כֵּיוָן דְּחוֹבָה הוּא — מַפֵּיק, אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule taught earlier on the דף, that food ברכות cannot be said for others by someone who already fulfilled his obligation, and asks about מצוה-related foods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברכה on מצה bread and on קידוש wine counts as a חובה, so it can be said for others, or as an ordinary food ברכה, so it cannot.

steps.title: רב פפי made קידוש again for his tenants
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רב פפי made קידוש for the students and then made it again for his tenants. This shows that one can say קידוש, including the wine ברכה, for others even after fulfilling his own obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב אשי said, 'When we were at רב פפי's house, he made קידוש for us. When his tenant farmers came in from the field, he made קידוש for them too.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a story. רב פפי made קידוש a second time for his workers, even though he had already fulfilled his own obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making קידוש a second time includes saying the wine ברכה again for others. This shows that the wine ברכה of קידוש is treated as part of the חובה. So the answer to the question is the first side: he can say it for others (מפיק).

keyTerms.meaning: His tenant farmers (אריסים), who work a field for a share of the crop

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the common practice that a person may make קידוש for others, such as family members or guests, even after he has already made קידוש for himself.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Ashi said:
When we were at the house of Rav Pappi,
he would make kiddush for us.
And when his tenant farmers would come from the field,
he would make kiddush for them.
phrases.notes: This is the key point: he had already done קידוש, and he did it again just for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1 using a story about what a אמורא actually did.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה on the wine of קידוש may be said for others even by someone who already fulfilled his own obligation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אשי's report about רב פפי repeating קידוש for his tenants.

steps.title: A ברייתא: guests, children, הלל, and מגילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one may not say המוציא for guests unless he eats with them. He may say it for his children to train them. For הלל and מגילה, he can be מוציא others even after he has already fulfilled his own obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person should not break bread and say the ברכה for guests unless he is eating with them. But he may do so for his children and household to train them in מצוות. And for הלל and מגילה, even if he has already fulfilled his obligation, he can be מוציא others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lays out the basic rules. A food ברכה is only said for others if you are eating too, and ברכות of a מצוה can be said for others anytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guest rule confirms that המוציא is a food ברכה, so someone who is not eating cannot say it for adults. Children are an exception because of חינוך, which means teaching them how to make ברכות. הלל and מגילה are מצוה obligations, so one person can always be מוציא another.

keyTerms.meaning: Break bread, meaning cut the bread and say המוציא for others
To train them (חינוך) in doing מצוות
The praise of תהלים 113 to 118, said on holidays
Takes others out of their obligation

steps.whatToRemember: Food ברכות such as המוציא can be said for others only if you are eating too, except for training children. ברכות of a מצוה, such as הלל, מגילה, and the wine of קידוש, can be said for others even after you have already fulfilled your own obligation.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person should not break bread for guests
phrases.notes: Breaking bread here means saying המוציא for them so they can eat.

phrases.english: unless he eats with them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל פּוֹרֵס הוּא לְבָנָיו וְלִבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ
phrases.english: but he may break bread for his children and his household members
in order to train them in מצוות.
And with hallel and the megillah,
even though he already fulfilled his obligation, he can discharge others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that sets out the general rules for food ברכות and מצוה ברכות, and rounds out the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No המוציא for guests unless you eat with them. You may say it for children to train them. For הלל and מגילה, you can be מוציא others even after you have already fulfilled your own obligation.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק ראוהו בית דין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the third פרק of ראש השנה, ראוהו בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק ראוהו בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק ראוהו בית דין. The next פרק begins after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said when finishing a פרק. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again. It is not part of the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the formula said when finishing a פרק
The name of the פרק: the בית דין saw it, meaning the new moon

phrases.english: We will return to you,
perek 'The court saw it'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the final ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק ראוהו בית דין is finished, and a new פרק follows.

steps.title: שופר on שבת: מקדש only, then רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens: when ראש השנה falls on שבת, they blew שופר only in the מקדש. After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי set up blowing wherever there is a בית דין. רבי אלעזר limits this to יבנה, and the חכמים disagree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ראש השנה falls on שבת, they blew the שופר in the מקדש but not in the rest of the land. After the מקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי set up that they should blow in every place that has a בית דין. רבי אלעזר said he set it up only for יבנה. The חכמים answered: יבנה and every place with a בית דין are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the opening משנה of the new פרק. It gives the rule for blowing שופר when ראש השנה falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the שופר is not blown on שבת, but the מקדש was an exception. After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי moved that exception to places with a בית דין. The argument is about how far his enactment reaches: only יבנה (רבי אלעזר), or any בית דין (the חכמים).

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the land, outside the מקדש
Set up a rule (made a תקנה)
The town where the סנהדרין sat after the חורבן

steps.confusionAlert: Here מדינה does not mean a country or state. It means everywhere outside the מקדש, including the rest of ירושלים.

phrases.english: The festival day of Rosh HaShanah
that happens to fall on Shabbat:
in the Temple they would blow the shofar,
but not in the rest of the land.
phrases.notes: Even the rest of ירושלים counts as 'the land' here. Only the מקדש itself was different.

phrases.english: Once the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai set up a rule
that they should blow in every place
that has a court in it.
Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai did not set it up
except in Yavne alone.
They said to him:
Yavne and every place are the same,
as long as it has a court in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק right after the הדרן in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה that falls on שבת, the שופר was blown only in the מקדש. After the חורבן it is blown wherever there is a בית דין (חכמים), or only in יבנה (רבי אלעזר).

steps.title: Jerusalem's advantage over Yavne
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that in ירושלים, any nearby city that could see, hear and come to ירושלים also blew. In יבנה, they blew only in the בית דין itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירושלים had one more advantage over יבנה. Any city that could see ירושלים, hear the blowing, was close, and could come there, would also blow. In יבנה they blew only in the בית דין itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on and compares ירושלים to יבנה. It says how far the שבת blowing reached in each place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושלים, the blowing reached the cities around it if they met all four conditions. In יבנה it was limited to the בית דין alone. So the enactment for יבנה was narrower than what ירושלים had in earlier times.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is able to come there

steps.whatToRemember: The rule has three levels: the מקדש (blowing on שבת), ירושלים with its nearby cities, and יבנה (only in the בית דין).

phrases.english: And furthermore, Jerusalem had this
advantage over Yavne:
that any city that could see and hear,
phrases.notes: He means a city that could see ירושלים and hear the שופר blown there.

phrases.english: and was close by, and could come there,
they would blow there too.
But in Yavne they would not blow
except in the court alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד זֹאת הָיְתָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יְתֵירָה עַל יַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by comparing ירושלים and יבנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ירושלים, nearby cities that could see, hear, were close and could come also blew. In יבנה, only the בית דין blew.

steps.title: What is the source for not blowing on Shabbat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that the שופר is not blown on שבת. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנא הני מילי is a request for a source, usually a פסוק. The question assumes the rule might come from the Torah itself.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: Gemara:
From where do we know these things?
phrases.notes: 'These things' means the rule that the שופר is not blown when ראש השנה falls on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for not blowing שופר on ראש השנה that falls on שבת.

steps.title: Two verses that seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא points to two פסוקים: one calls the day a 'remembrance of blowing,' and the other calls it a 'day of blowing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר לחמא said in the name of רבי חמא בר חנינא: One פסוק says 'a rest, a remembrance of blowing.' Another פסוק says 'a day of blowing it shall be for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer starts by setting two פסוקים against each other. It sets up the resolution that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זכרון תרועה' suggests we only remember the blowing without doing it. 'יום תרועה' suggests we actually blow. The answer will come from explaining when each פסוק applies.

keyTerms.meaning: One פסוק says (opens two פסוקים that seem to clash)

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Lachma said
that Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
One verse says:
"A day of rest, a remembrance of blowing."
And another verse says:
"It shall be a day of blowing for you"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 7 by bringing two פסוקים that seem to clash.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source lies in the gap between 'זכרון תרועה' and 'יום תרועה'.

steps.title: שבת versus a weekday
steps.stepSummary: The two פסוקים are reconciled: 'remembrance' is for ראש השנה on שבת, and 'day of blowing' is for ראש השנה on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. The first פסוק is talking about יום טוב that falls on שבת, when we only remember. The second פסוק is talking about יום טוב that falls on a weekday, when we blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the two פסוקים by giving each one a different case. This finishes the source for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק is given its own situation, so the two no longer clash. The result is that not blowing on שבת looks like a Torah rule. רבא will challenge exactly this point next.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... here (each source fits a different case)

phrases.english: It is not a problem:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: here, it is about a Yom Tov that falls on Shabbat;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the first פסוק, 'זכרון תרועה', where we only remember the blowing.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּחוֹל.
phrases.english: there, it is about a Yom Tov that falls on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between the two פסוקים from step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים contradict each other about whether we blow.
steps.terutzMaskana: On שבת we only remember the blowing. On a weekday we blow.

steps.title: רבא: then how could they blow in the Temple?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the source: if the Torah forbids blowing on שבת, the מקדש should not have blown either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If it is a Torah rule, how do we blow in the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer just given. If the Torah itself says not to blow on שבת, the משנה's rule that they blew in the מקדש makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Torah rule based on a פסוק would apply everywhere, including the מקדש. Yet the משנה says they did blow in the מקדש on שבת. That suggests the ban is not from the Torah at all.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If it is a Torah rule,
how do we blow in the Temple?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from the פסוקים in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah ban would include the מקדש, but the משנה says they blew there on שבת.

steps.title: רבא: blowing is not even a מלאכה
steps.stepSummary: רבא's second challenge: blowing שופר is not a מלאכה, so there is nothing for a פסוק to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, blowing is not a מלאכה, so why would a פסוק be needed to exclude it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second problem with the source. The proof for his claim comes in the next lines of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק would only be needed to forbid blowing on שבת if blowing were a forbidden מלאכה. But blowing is not a מלאכה at all. So the Torah has nothing to forbid, and the ban must come from the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden kind of work on שבת or יום טוב

steps.whyThisMatters: Taken together, רבא's two challenges show that not blowing on שבת is a rule of the חכמים, not of the Torah.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
it is not a forbidden labor,
that a verse should be needed to exclude it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to רבא's first one in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from the פסוקים in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blowing is not a מלאכה, so a פסוק would never be needed to forbid it on שבת.

steps.title: A teaching from the school of שמואל shows that blowing שופר is not a forbidden labor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from דבי שמואל teaches that the פסוק 'do no work of labor' excludes blowing שופר and removing bread from the oven, because they are skills, not labors.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of שמואל taught: 'You shall do no work of labor.' This leaves out blowing the שופר and removing bread from the oven, because that is a skill and not a labor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for רבא's second challenge, the claim that blowing שופר is not a מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא argued that no פסוק is needed to forbid blowing on שבת, since blowing is not a מלאכה to begin with. This ברייתא confirms it: the Torah's ban on labor does not include blowing שופר, because blowing is a חכמה (a skill) and not a מלאכה. So the source from Step 9 now looks even weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: Work of labor, the kind of work forbidden on a יום טוב
Removing baked bread from the oven
A skill or know-how, not physical labor

phrases.english: As the school of Shmuel taught:
"You shall do no work of labor"
this leaves out blowing the shofar and removing bread from the oven,
since it is a skill and not a labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's claim in Step 11 that blowing שופר is not a מלאכה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that blowing שופר is not a מלאכה, so no פסוק is needed to exclude it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of דבי שמואל on 'כל מלאכת עבודה לא תעשו'.

steps.title: רבא's new answer: the Torah permits it, but the Rabbis forbade it
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the פסוק-based source and says that דאורייתא blowing on שבת is permitted. Only the רבנן decreed against it, following רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: By Torah law it is completely permitted. It is the רבנן who made a decree against it, following רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: After challenging the earlier source, רבא gives his own explanation for why we do not blow on שבת: it is a rabbinic rule, not a Torah rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of רבא's challenges assumed the ban was from the Torah. By making it only a גזירה of the רבנן, the problem of the מקדש blowing is no longer a clash with a Torah ban, and there is no need for a פסוק to exclude something that is not a מלאכה. The reason for the decree comes in the next step from רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: signals dropping the earlier approach
Who made a decree (a rabbinic safeguard)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the Torah forbids blowing on שבת. According to רבא, the Torah allows it, and the whole ban comes from the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the accepted reason why we do not blow שופר when ראש השנה falls on שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
By Torah law, it is completely permitted,
and it is the Rabbis who made a decree against it,
following Rabbah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in Steps 10 to 12 with a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the ban from Torah law to rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on blowing on שבת comes from a פסוק ('remembrance of blowing').
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah permits blowing on שבת. The ban is a rabbinic גזירה.

steps.title: רבה's reason: someone might carry the שופר to an expert
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains the גזירה. Everyone must hear שופר, but not everyone knows how to blow, so a person might carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים on the way to an expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבה said: Everyone is obligated in blowing שופר, but not everyone knows how to blow. So the רבנן made a decree, in case a person takes it in his hand to go learn from an expert and carries it four אמות in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבה's statement that gives the reason behind the rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is not about the blowing itself, which is fine. The worry is that the blowing will lead to carrying, which is a real Torah violation of שבת. To protect against this, the רבנן banned the blowing altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree, out of concern that
Four cubits, the distance that makes carrying forbidden

phrases.english: For Rabbah said:
Everyone is obligated in blowing the shofar,
but not everyone is skilled in blowing the shofar.
It is a decree, in case he takes it in his hand
and goes to the expert to learn,
and carries it four cubits in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reason behind the decree רבא mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן banned blowing שופר on שבת out of concern that someone would carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים to an expert.

steps.title: The same reason applies to לולב and מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the same worry about carrying explains why לולב is not taken and מגילה is not read on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the reason for לולב, and this is the reason for מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא widens רבה's reason and applies it to two other מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like שופר, people might carry a לולב or a מגילה to an expert on שבת. So one rabbinic concern explains three different rules.
steps.whatToRemember: Blowing on שבת is permitted by the Torah. The רבנן banned it, as with לולב and מגילה, because someone might carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: And this is the reason for the lulav,
and this is the reason for the Megillah.
phrases.notes: He means: why we don't take a לולב or read the מגילה when the day falls on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבה's reason to other מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same concern about carrying is why לולב and מגילה are not done on שבת.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה and starts a ברייתא: once ראש השנה fell on שבת and people from all the cities gathered.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'After the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי instituted,' and so on. The רבנן taught: Once ראש השנה fell on שבת, and all the cities were gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and sets the scene for a story. This step is setting up the conversation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new section. The ברייתא gives the background to the תקנה of blowing on שבת after the חורבן. Here it only describes the setting: ראש השנה on שבת with a large gathering.

phrases.english: After the Temple was destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted, etc.
The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת חָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Once Rosh Hashanah fell on Shabbat,
and people from all the cities were gathering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of why there is no blowing on שבת and moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the background story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says to blow, בני בתירה want to discuss it
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי tells בני בתירה, 'Let us blow!' They answer, 'Let us discuss it first.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to בני בתירה: Let us blow! They said to him: Let us discuss it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story's conversation begins. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי wants to blow the שופר on שבת, and בני בתירה want to discuss first whether it is allowed. The story continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי wants to act right away. בני בתירה want to discuss the question before acting. This tension sets up his reply, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of Beteira, leading Torah authorities of the time

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לִבְנֵי בְּתִירָה:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to the sons of Beteira:
Let us blow!
They said to him: Let us discuss it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לִבְנֵי בְּתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי proposes blowing on שבת, and בני בתירה ask to discuss it first.

steps.title: Blow first, discuss later, then no discussion
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי tells בני בתירה to blow first and discuss afterward. After the blowing, he refuses to reopen the question because the act is already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Let us blow, and afterward we will discuss. After they blew, they said to him: Let us discuss! He said to them: The horn has already been heard in יבנה, and we do not argue after the act is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא story from the last step ends here. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי gets the שופר blown on שבת before any debate can stop it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני בתירה wanted to discuss whether to blow, which could have stopped the blowing. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reversed the order: first the act, then the talk. Once it was done in public, he told them the matter was settled, so his תקנה was in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us discuss and debate the question
We do not argue against something after it has already been done

steps.whatToRemember: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי set up the practice of blowing on שבת in יבנה by acting first. Once it was done, it was not reopened for debate.

phrases.english: He said to them: Let us blow,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, and "them" is בני בתירה, from the previous step.

phrases.english: and afterward we will discuss.
After they blew, they said to him: Let us discuss!

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּבָר נִשְׁמְעָה קֶרֶן בְּיַבְנֶה,
phrases.english: He said to them: The horn has already been heard in יבנה,
and we do not argue after the act is done.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: נִתְקַע, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָדוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא story begun in steps 16 and 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blowing in יבנה was done first, and it was not reopened for debate afterward.

steps.title: Only יבנה, or every place with a בית דין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי אלעזר says the תקנה was only for יבנה, and the חכמים say it applies to יבנה and any place with a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made the תקנה only for יבנה. They said to him: Both יבנה and any place that has a בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes an argument about how far the תקנה reaches. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר limits the תקנה to יבנה alone. The חכמים answer him that it covers any place with a בית דין. The next step asks how this answer differs from what the משנה already said.

keyTerms.meaning: He set up a rule (made a תקנה)
The town where the great בית דין sat after the חורבן

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי did not set up the rule
except in יבנה alone.
They said to him: Both יבנה
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים in the משנה, answering רבי אלעזר.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and any place that has a court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי אֶלָּא בְּיַבְנֶה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא story and goes back to the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: only יבנה. חכמים: יבנה and any place with a בית דין.

steps.title: The חכמים seem to repeat the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the חכמים' statement says the same thing as the תנא קמא, so why repeat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: "They said to him": that is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the חכמים' answer to רבי אלעזר looks like a repeat of what the first part of the משנה already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's first, unnamed opinion already said the תקנה applies anywhere there is a בית דין. If the חכמים say the same thing, their line seems to add nothing. The גמרא expects every line in a משנה to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: "They said to him": that is the same as the first תנא!
phrases.notes: Here "they said to him" is the גמרא pointing to the חכמים' line in the משנה, not a new speaker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים' statement just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' statement in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to repeat the תנא קמא's opinion, so it would add nothing new.

steps.title: They differ about a temporary בית דין
steps.stepSummary: The difference between the תנא קמא and the חכמים is a בית דין that is only there temporarily.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a court that is there only by chance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions are not the same. They disagree about a temporary בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא lets the שופר be blown on שבת even where a בית דין is only there for a while. The חכמים compare every place to יבנה, so they allow it only where a fixed, permanent בית דין sits. So the חכמים' line does add something.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary court, one that is there only by chance

steps.confusionAlert: Compared with the תנא קמא, the חכמים are the stricter side: they require a permanent בית דין like the one in יבנה. They are still more lenient than רבי אלעזר, who allows only יבנה itself.

phrases.english: The difference between them is
phrases.notes: "Them" means the תנא קמא and the חכמים who answered רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: a court that is there only by chance.
phrases.notes: He means a בית דין that is not fixed in one place. The תנא קמא allows blowing there, and the חכמים do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים simply repeated the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא includes a temporary בית דין. The חכמים require a permanent one like יבנה.

steps.title: Quoting the חכמים again to bring רב הונא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים' line again to introduce a new teaching from רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Both יבנה and any place that has a בית דין. רב הונא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the חכמים' words again because רב הונא is about to say something about them. His statement comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words were already quoted in step 19, but here they are repeated for a new purpose. Before, the question was how they differ from the תנא קמא. Now they open a new teaching from רב הונא about this same line.

phrases.english: They said to him: Both יבנה

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and any place that has a court.
רב הונא said:
phrases.notes: His actual statement comes on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֶחָד יַבְנֶה וְאֶחָד כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בֵּית דִּין. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the חכמים' line from step 19 to start a new discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: רב הונא is about to comment on the חכמים' line.
